title: Why Is My Heating Running but Not Warming the House?

seo.title: Why Is My Heating Running but Not Warming the House?
seo.meta_description: If the heating system runs but the house stays cold, check actual output, airflow, filter, distribution, and operating pattern before touching gas or internal controls.
seo.search_intent: Diagnose a heating system that starts or runs but does not deliver enough heat, distinct from equipment that never starts.

excerpt: This problem begins after the system has already started. If you can hear equipment or feel circulation but the home does not gain temperature, separate heat production, airflow, and distribution.
content_html:
First confirm what is actually running and what temperature the system is delivering. “Not heating” can mean lukewarm supply air, cold radiators, or simply failure to reach the thermostat target.

Check filter and airflow on forced-air systems

A severely loaded filter, blocked returns, or many closed registers can restrict distribution and contribute to protective shutdowns.

Heat-pump air may feel only warm

Heat pumps often deliver lower-temperature air than combustion furnaces. Judge whether the home maintains setpoint and whether brief defrost cycles return to normal operation.

Compare radiators by zone

A radiator cold at the top may contain air; a completely cold unit may have a valve or circulation problem. If every radiator is cold, look upstream at the central system.

Notice whether the equipment stops too soon

Short cycles, error codes, new noise, or repeated restarts can prevent adequate heat delivery. Do not bypass limit switches or safety controls.

Stop for fuel or electrical warning signs

Gas odor, a carbon-monoxide alarm, smoke, strong electrical odor, or repeated breaker trips require shutdown or evacuation as appropriate and qualified help.

If the system runs but can no longer maintain a temperature it previously reached, that loss of performance is meaningful evidence for service.

faq.question: Does lukewarm air mean a heat pump is broken?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Heat pumps can deliver cooler-feeling air than furnaces; check whether the home maintains setpoint.

faq.question: Should I close vents to force heat into other rooms?
faq.answer: Not as a general rule; closing many registers can disrupt required airflow.

faq.question: How is this different from “heat won’t turn on”?
faq.answer: Here the equipment starts or circulates but does not provide enough heat, so the troubleshooting path is different.
